title: fix(sim): fixture laws pad each arc chord by its sagitta
body:
Found while gating #339 slice 2 (PR #492): the fixture box laws judged an arc by its **inscribed** chords at the bare band radius, so steel within the arc's sagitta (about 0.01 mm on R30) was missed. This applied to every fixture.

## What changed
New `crates/sim/src/verify/arc_bulge.rs` (`Bulge`, `ARC_PAD` = 1e-3).

**The pad.** For each chord, with ψ = |θ|/2 and θ = sweep/n (the same equal steps `arc_chords` cuts):
- **Across the chord:** r(1 − cos ψ), the sagitta.
- **Along the chord:** r(ψ − sin ψ).

These bound the true point against the chord point at the same sweep fraction for ψ ≤ π/2. Past a half turn, 2r is used for both. Every arc chord adds `ARC_PAD`, because arc centres sit on the 1 µm lattice.

**XY arcs (box laws, `stack_span`):** the band radius grows by `hypot(across, along) + ARC_PAD`. A helix's z between joints is already exact.

**XZ/YZ arcs:**
- The radius grows by `along·|t_h| + across·|n_h| + ARC_PAD`.
- The z window is the arc's true range between joints. Builder-split arcs are Z-monotone, so the strict-dip silence for a lead arc landing tangent on a face is kept.
- An arc that turns past its circle's top or bottom inside a chord gets that piece's window carried to the extremum ± ARC_PAD.

**Posed sweep (`posed_steel`):** an arc move's capsules grow by `Bulge::deviation()`. The interval travel already covered all but about 1e-4 mm; the pad makes the bound hold for any interval length.

**Straight moves get a pad of exactly 0.0,** so every straight verdict is bit-identical.

**Bad arcs fail closed:** a non-finite centre or radius gives a NaN pad, which the predicates read as a hit.

`docs/decisions/491-arc-sagitta.md`

## How tested
New sim `fixture_arc_sagitta` (10 tests). These four fail on main and pass now:
- **The issue's repro:** R30 arc, r3 flute, 3 chords, sagitta 0.00937, box half a sagitta inside the true reach → Flute. The same arc as a rapid → Rapid.
- The holder band is padded too.
- An XZ arc bulging sideways reports.
- An unsplit XZ arc dipping past its chords reports.

These also pass, as pins:
- Steel 0.002 mm beyond the true reach stays clean.
- A YZ arc bulging sideways reports.
- An XZ arc landing tangent on a face stays silent, while 0.001 deeper hits.
- A posed arc within its sagitta reports.
- Straight moves keep their verdicts.
- The apex sits mid-chord.

**Gates:**
- `scripts/gate.sh quick upstream/main` (all sim suites) is green.
- The full camcraft-app suite, all 170 binaries, is green with **no existing verdict changed**. After the final syntax-only edit, sim in full and the app fixture, rotary, carried, posed-contact, arc-entry and posting suites were re-run, all green.
- `clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean.

**Note:** #476's `mesh_steel` has its own `ARC_PAD` and can read `Bulge::deviation` once both land. #413 is the same family in the field engine and envelope scan, and stays its own issue.

Changelog: Fixture collision laws pad each arc chord by its sagitta, so steel within an arc's bulge is no longer missed (#491)

Fixes #491

title: fix(sim): judge a gouge with tol of lateral slack at a wall
body:
## What changed

The program sim's gouge verdict judged each column by height alone, at its centre. A height verdict's normal-distance tolerance is `tol * cos(slope)`, which is zero at a vertical wall. So a column whose centre sits a few microns inside a wall, reached by a tool that finishes that wall within tolerance, was charged the wall's whole height, and the post gate refused a correct program.

- New `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/wall_slack.rs`: a gouge candidate (a column more than `tol` below the part's top at its centre) is re-judged against the lowest part top within `tol` of its centre. That is the centre plus an eight-direction ring at radius `tol`, and air counts as lowest. If the column is within `tol` of that lowest top, it is clean. Otherwise it is a gouge, charged at the centre's own depth as before.
- Both engines use it: the column engine (`deviate`) and the field arm (`deviate_field`), keeping the stage-C parity law.
- Rest is unchanged: it is still judged against the centre's own top.
- The extra cost is paid only when gouge candidates exist. A clean program costs nothing extra.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/299-wall-column-gouge.md`. It covers why the slack is `tol` and not the issue's `gate_tol(DEV_TOL, cell)`, and the other options that were dropped.

## Readings (current main 5fd2b93)

- The issue's exact 2D Contour repro (model stock, 10 mm deep) **no longer reproduces on main**: the gate is clean before and after this change. It is kept as a regression test.
- 3D Finish, `BN-0600`, kind defaults, model stock (the issue's MCP job): before, `gouge: ... 1 cell(s), worst 10.21 mm at (16.69, -24.91, z 9.79)`. Probing that column, its centre is 1-3 um inside the D's wall, with air beyond. After: no gouge. The post is still blocked, by the generator's own `ShankHit` warnings, which is a separate matter.
- 3D Finish in the issue's 70 x 70 x 27 box at z -7: before, 37 cells, worst 22.01 mm at (-26.56, 13.94). After: 0 gouge cells.

## Tests

- `crates/sim/tests/wall_slack.rs` (new, 5 tests):
  - `a_column_a_few_microns_inside_a_finished_wall_is_not_a_gouge`: both engines, with a floor beside the wall and with air beside it. This test fails on main.
  - `the_old_law_charged_that_column_the_whole_wall`
  - `a_real_gouge_into_a_wall_still_convicts_at_its_full_depth`: covers 50 um, 12 um and 1 mm intrusions, in both engines, and checks the full 15 mm depth and location.
  - `a_floor_gouge_away_from_walls_is_unchanged`
  - `rest_beside_a_wall_keeps_the_centres_own_top`
- `crates/app/tests/wall_column_gouge.rs` (new, 3 tests):
  - `a_3d_finish_on_the_users_part_reads_no_gouge_at_its_wall`: fails on main.
  - `a_3d_finish_in_the_users_box_stock_reads_no_gouge_at_its_wall`: fails on main.
  - `the_issues_contour_on_model_stock_reads_no_gouge`
- Gate results:
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-sim`: all green.
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-app` (all 169 binaries, debug): all green.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.
- Release `--ignored` lanes:
  - sim `hidden_rest_banded`, app `operations` and `rotary_field_parity`: green.
  - app `stock_engine_agreement` has 2 tests (`both_engines_judge_every_golden_program_alike`, `the_feed_sampler_reads_every_golden_program_alike`) that **fail identically on upstream/main** (6467 FINDING lines, for example `contour_disc_hole.cl` column (46.25, -4.25) and `finish3d_scallop_plateau.cl+bull` engagement). This is pre-existing and not caused by this PR. Diffing the findings between main and this branch shows 5 lines changed: field-arm micro-readings on `finish3d_project_dome.cl` (field dev -0.011 to -0.016 on the slope) now read clean instead of gouge. That is the expected slope allowance (at most `tol * tan(slope)`). No column-engine verdict changed, and no golden changed.

## Not exercised

- GUI Deviate view, by eye.
- A real cut.
- `kernel::measure` / `measure_field` (the per-op reports, not the post gate) keep the centre-only law.
- #303 (chamfer/deburr false gouge) is **not** fixed by this. Its bevel is a sloped cut 0.74-3.8 mm deep, far past a 10 um slack, and needs the op-owns-its-break law the issue describes.

Changelog: The post gate no longer refuses a correct program for a gouge at a wall: a sim column within the 0.01 mm tolerance of a vertical wall is judged against the floor beside it, while a cut past that still refuses (#299)

Fixes #299

title: fix(post): built-in VMC and tilt-head stroke bands in program coordinates
body:
## What changed

The built-in **VMC 3-axis** (`assets/machines/vmc.mch`) and **Tilt-head 5-axis** (`assets/machines/tilthead.mch`) stated machine-frame strokes (Z `-500..0`, X `±300`, Y `±250`), but the limit checker (`app::machine::check_document`) reads travel bands in **program coordinates through the work offset**. Every move above the Z0 work origin was out of stroke, so no program posted on the built-in VMC.

Fix: restate both files the way the Tormach files already are (b189c960): a slide of stroke L is `-L..L`, the full stroke either way, because the file cannot know where the work offset sits along the slide. Now Z `-500..500`, X `-600..600`, Y `-500..500`. No checker code changed. The rule is written down in the `app::machine` module doc and `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`. Test-fixture comments in `tilt.rs`, `rotary_verify.rs` and `post_not_judged.rs` that cited the old `-500..0` band were updated (comments only). The decision is recorded in `docs/decisions/457-vmc-z-stroke.md`.

## How tested

- New `crates/app/tests/vmc_stroke.rs`:
  - `a_plate_contour_on_the_built_in_vmc_passes_the_stroke_and_posts`: the issue's repro (2D Contour on a 1 mm plate, clearance Z 26, built-in VMC as the document machine). `check_document` is clean, `verification_report` has no problems, and `post_setup` posts. On the old `vmc.mch` this fails with the reported `... reaches 1.000 in Z, the stroke is -500.000..0.000` flood.
  - `a_clearance_past_the_vmc_column_still_refuses_by_name`: clearance Z 520 is refused with `2D Contour1: move N reaches 520.000 in Z, the stroke is -500.000..500.000`, and the post is refused.
- These suites all passed (debug): `vmc_stroke`, `machine`, `machine_library`, `posting`, `tormach_post`, `tormach_machines`, `tilt`, `rotary_verify`, `post_not_judged`, `setup_sheet`, `inverted_post`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- `lathe.mch` (X `0..320`, Z `-615..0`) and `millturn.mch` (X `0..650`, Z `-620..0`) are unchanged. They still state one-sided bands that may refuse approach moves in front of the face. They need their own decision.
- I did not run the headless MCP repro (`camcraft-cli mcp`), the GUI, or the ui crate suites. The ui crate is untouched, and its tests reference the VMC by name only.
- Posted G-code does not change for any machine. The script mirror carries no linear travel, so the golden NC files are unaffected.

Changelog: The built-in VMC 3-axis and Tilt-head 5-axis machines state their strokes in program coordinates (full stroke each way), so ordinary programs post instead of being refused for every retract above Z0.

Fixes #457
